strategies.deleteConfirm: Delete the strategy "{{name}}" and all its versions? If it is active, its sleeve targets are released. This cannot be undone.

modeHint.active: This strategy sets your sleeve targets, and its signals reach your inbox and your phone.
modeHint.shadow: Evaluated and logged next to the active strategy, never notified. Its signals appear only here.

empty.title: No strategy yet
empty.body: Start with the guided setup, which asks a few plain questions, or use New strategy for the full form with every target empty, so nothing fires until you set the numbers.

editor.saved: Saved. Earlier versions stay as they were.

form.name: Name
form.sleevesHint: Members are ISINs or instrument tags, separated by commas. Targets are percentages of the portfolio; bands are percentage points around the target. Leave a number empty until you have decided.
form.principlesHint: One per line. The agent gets them word for word and must say when its advice departs from them.

hint.allocator: Splits new money over the sleeves: shortfalls against the targets first, the rest by target weight. Whole units; the change is shown.
hint.trim: Sells only what is above the target of a sleeve past its trim level or band, never below the target, with the realized result of each sale.
hint.rebalance: Brings every sleeve back inside its band with as few trades as possible, using new money before selling.

history.one: Only one version so far. Every save adds one.
history.caption: Changes from version {{older}} to version {{newer}}

orders.title: Orders from your strategy
orders.intro: Proposed by a calculator. Enter the price and fees you actually paid, then confirm each one; until then nothing changes in your holdings.

wizard.title: Guided setup

name.title: Name your plan
name.intro: A strategy is your plan written down: how your money should be split and when Folio should warn you. This guide asks a few plain questions and writes it for you. You can change everything afterwards.
name.label: What do you call this plan?

groups.title: Put your holdings into groups
groups.intro: A group (Folio calls it a sleeve) is a part of your portfolio with one job, for example 'World shares', 'Bonds' or 'Themes'. Make a few groups and choose one for each holding.
groups.caption: Your holdings and their groups
groups.noHoldings: You have no holdings with an ISIN yet, so there is nothing to group. You can still make groups and add holdings later in the full form.
groups.noIsin: {{count}} holding without an ISIN is left out; add the ISIN on its page to include it.
groups.unassigned: Not in any group yet, so left out of the targets: {{names}}.

targets.title: Set a target for each group
targets.intro: How much of your portfolio, in percent, should each group be? The targets must add up to 100. If you are unsure, start from today's mix and adjust later.

strictness.title: How strictly should Folio watch the targets?
strictness.intro: A group is 'off target' when its share moves away from its target. Choose how many percentage points away Folio warns you (first the soft limit, then the firm one).
strictness.detail: Warn at {{soft}} points off target, firmly at {{hard}} points.

alerts.title: Which alerts do you want?
alerts.intro: Alerts appear in your inbox. Folio never trades for you; it only tells you.
alerts.drift: A group has moved away from its target
alerts.trim: A group has grown far above its target (time to consider taking profit)
alerts.drawdown: A holding has fallen from its highest price
alerts.concentration: One company is too large across all my funds (needs the funds' holdings uploaded)
alerts.more: Rules about interest rates, correlations and price levels are in the full form.

plan.title: Regular investing (optional)
plan.intro: If you put in a fixed amount on a schedule, Folio can remind you before it is due and suggest which group should get it. If you invest when you like, skip this.
plan.use: I invest a fixed amount regularly

principles.title: Your rules of thumb
principles.intro: Principles are short sentences about how you invest. The AI agent reads them when it reviews your portfolio.

review.title: Check and save
review.intro: This is what the guide will create. Nothing is saved until you press the button, and every part can be changed afterwards.
review.group_one: {{name}}: target {{target}} %, {{count}} holding, warning at {{soft}} points off.
review.group_other: {{name}}: target {{target}} %, {{count}} holdings, warning at {{soft}} points off.
review.drift: Firm warning when a group is off target by the hard limit ({{hard}} points).
review.trim: Take-profit alert when a group is {{over}} points above its target.
review.drawdown: Alert when a holding falls {{pct}} % from its peak.
review.concentration: Alert when one company is over {{pct}} % of the portfolio.
review.plan: Reminder for your {{cadence}} investment of {{amount}} EUR.
review.off: Save it switched off, so I can look at it first (recommended).
review.active: Save it and make it the active strategy. It then sets the targets of your groups, and any other active strategy becomes a shadow.

wizard.madeWith: Made with the guided setup. Everything can be changed here.

strategyReview.title: Quarterly review
strategyReview.notOver: This quarter is not over yet, so the review is a preview and cannot be sent to the inbox.
strategyReview.alreadyPosted: This quarter already has its item in the inbox.
strategyReview.noStrategy: Make a strategy active to get a review.
strategyReview.sleevesCaption: Drift of each sleeve from its target
strategyReview.daysWithData: {{count}} day(s) of portfolio history in this quarter.

backtest.intro: Try the rules on the past: for each trading day in the range, Folio checks them against the portfolio as it was that day and lists when they would have fired, with the value that made them fire (for a drift rule, how far from target in percentage points). Nothing is saved or sent.
backtest.summary: {{days}} trading days checked against version {{version}}; the rules would have fired {{count}} time(s).
backtest.rulesCaption: What each rule did in the range
backtest.firingsCaption: The days the rules would have fired
backtest.none: Nothing would have fired in this range.
